titolo: How Knight Capital Lost $440,000,000 in 45 Minutes

copertina.immagine: A single dark server in a vast empty trading office, glowing red and cracking open, with golden coins pouring out onto the floor and a giant clock behind it

shots.voce: Four hundred forty million dollars. Gone in forty-five minutes. One company, one broken software update, and nobody able to stop it.
shots.immagine: A towering stack of golden coins melting into a glowing red puddle in front of a huge clock face, dark studio background

shots.voce: August first, twenty twelve. Knight Capital is among the biggest traders on Wall Street, handling a large share of American stock orders.
shots.immagine: A glossy 3D skyscraper trading floor at dawn, faceless figures at desks with glowing blue screens showing abstract charts without readable text

shots.voce: That morning, engineers roll out new trading software to eight servers. But one server never receives the update. It still runs old code.
shots.immagine: A row of eight servers in a dark room, seven glowing blue and one dim server in the middle with a faint gold light

shots.voce: Before the opening bell, ninety-seven automated emails flag a problem. They are not treated as alarms. At nine thirty, the market opens.
shots.immagine: A pile of floating glowing envelopes drifting unread above an empty desk, a large clock behind them pointing to nine thirty

shots.voce: A reused setting wakes a dead program, unused for years. The eighth server buys and sells at full speed, never knowing when to stop.
shots.immagine: A single server with a glowing red button on its front, an old dusty gear mechanism inside it spinning to life

shots.voce: The machine buys high and sells low, again and again. In total, about four million trades hit one hundred fifty-four stocks.
shots.immagine: A massive wall of trading screens with red zigzag lines and no readable text, a stream of golden coins flying out of a server into the dark
